intro: Seattle's public sauna scene is mostly mobile and on the water: wood-fired saunas parked at Alki Beach, Golden Gardens and Lincoln Park, where the cold plunge is Puget Sound, plus a floating sauna on Lake Union. Park-based saunas depend on permits, so locations can shift.

venues.name: Bywater Sauna
venues.neighborhood: Alki Beach, Golden Gardens, Old Stove (Ballard, Oct-Jun); Leschi currently closed
venues.cold_plunge: Open water (Puget Sound) or cool air
venues.schedule: Mixed; under-18 only with prior notice and a guardian.
venues.notes: Book ahead; limited spots per session. Bring your own towel.

venues.name: Sauna Moon Seattle
venues.address: Alki Beach Park, Seattle, WA 98116 (exact spot in booking confirmation)
venues.schedule: Unknown. Site lists Thursday-Saturday at Alki; permit-dependent.
venues.notes: Unlimited membership $100/month. Sessions are tentative until park permits are confirmed.

venues.name: Seattle Sauna (floating, Lake Union)
venues.cold_plunge: Cold bucket shower and outdoor shower (no plunge tub)
venues.schedule: Mixed guided social sessions, up to 10 guests. Open year-round.
venues.notes: Towels, water and changing rooms provided. Sessions stay dockside.

venues.name: Good Day Sauna (Lincoln Park)
venues.drop_in_price: $35 (implied by the venue's 5-pack: $150, "$5 off every session")
venues.notes: Fits up to 15 people. Iki wood stove.

venues.name: Wild Haus Floating Saunas
venues.address: 10 E Allison St, Seattle, WA (meeting point)
venues.drop_in_price: Unknown (third-party listings disagree; check booking page)
venues.notes: A sauna boat cruise rather than a classic drop-in; booking page describes a two-hour cruise. Pricier, special-occasion option.
